If I remember correctly, Cassini was not 100% sterilized before launch (only the Huygens probe), so rather than risk Cassini crashing into Enceladus (a moon with known liquid water jets) and contaminating it, they are "safely discarding" Cassini in Saturn's atmosphere.

Well if the Huygens was attached to Cassini, then it was contaminated also. And why would they be worried about it crashing, just put it in an orbit where that wouldn't happen.

The problem with a parking orbit (around Saturn or the Sun) is that you have to then track the craft to make sure nothing else that is sent that way will collide with it. When we sent Cassini to Saturn, we literally had it turn itself around and use its main dish as a fairing in case it hit ring debris during the braking maneuver.

Also, Cassini also has a RTG for power. As a parked Cassini fails and systems start failing, whatever is preventing that RTG from exploding into radioactive fun can fail, sending the craft on an impossible to predict trajectory, probably in many pieces, now covered in radioactive isotopes.
